evidence: Plan item 1.6 (docs/AGENT_PLAN.md, 'The A+ ceiling: what the validation can still measure'): on the paired cases the engines alone (arm A+) score close to 1, because most of a case score is facts a fixed rule gets right, so the case score could not show a model adding to the engines, and no dev case put A+'s fixed joining rules (validation/armA.js runArmSweep) in question. The plan names four situations where those rules are ambiguous or wrong: two features at once, a signal at 2.5–4σ, evidence that two tools read differently, and a choice only the user can make. After the change, five dev cases cover them, each tried with arms A, A+ and D on the dev set; their scores and where A+ misses are in the PR, validation/baseline/arm-a-dev.json and the validation/__tests__/arms.test.js pins, and kept out of this record, which the author of the held-out matches may read. Every earlier case, dev and test, builds byte for byte as before (TEST_SET_SHA256 unchanged), and a re-run of the earlier dev records equals each of them apart from protocol and commit. Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19.
proposed_fix: Five dev cases, each judgment: true with a situation and devOnly until its held-out match exists, their parameters apart in validation/judgmentCases.js and built by validation/cases.js: two features at once (jahn_teller with offCentre: Jahn–Teller octahedra whose centre is also off-centred); a signal at 2.5–4σ (zone_boundary with weak: true and no decoy: one weak cell-doubling order, one seed on each side of the 3σ bar by an outcome-neutral rule); two tools read differently (offcentre with wells: 8: eight-site <111> off-centring); a choice only the user can make (the new kind elongated_clusters: octahedral clusters elongated along a random axis, whose split shell the Workbench joins and asks about; since protocol 2026-10-19.8 A+ takes its cluster windows from that same shell reading, so on the score this case is the subset's control). Beside them: the report's judgment table (report.js renderJudgment, read from truth.judgment); the split test lets a judgment case use a paired kind's options and keeps the test set unchanged; the holdout scan never lets a judgment case remove a test token; validation/judgment-spec.md, the spec the author of the held-out matches works from, with no dev value, result or arm score (validation/__tests__/judgment.test.js scans it); PROTOCOL_VERSION 2026-10-19.9. The held-out matches come later, from a fresh author who never sees the dev results, in a separate PR, on the user's decision. Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19; the user may reverse it.
